newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks briskly shed points at open.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks briskly shed points at open.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE

* Toronto stocks extended Friday's slide at Monday's open, deepening losses as New York fell. * Nearly all of 14 sectors down. * 7 million shares traded worth C$114 million.
A trader added that Toronto's market looked set to decline after recent record-setting gains. "I think we're in a little bit of a corrective phase."
All of Toronto's 14 sectors succumbed to weakness, led by key golds, utilities, conglomerates, pipelines and banks.
Losing issues outnumbered gainers 249 to 179, while 201 traded flat.
Despite heavy trading value, few stocks sparked investor interest. "It's the Monday blahs," the trader said.
--- HOT STOCKS ---

* Oxford Properties Group Inc jumped 0.40 to 34 in very light trading after Prudential Insurance Co of America said on Monday its Canadian arm agreed to sell its Canadian real estate portfolio to a joint venture of Oxford and GE Capital Canada Inc for C$455.8 million.
* Telecommunications conglomerate BCE Inc, Canada's largest publicly traded company, dropped 0.85 to 41.40 in heavy dealings.
((Lydia Zajc, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8109))
Toronto's key stock index slipped more than 50 points at Monday's open as North American investors nervously eyed Tuesday's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan.

Market players sold off some holdings after last week's strong gains and ahead of Greenspan's comments on the U.S. economy, said Montreal-based strategist Bill Ram. "A little breather is not unusual, considering what's been going on."
"The market's really looking for an excuse to go down," he added. Ram noted that heavyweight interest-sensitive stocks, such as banks, were hit by profit-taking.
